subtopics.content: a. Definition and branches of agricultural science
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define agricultural science and state its branches

subtopics.content: b. Importance of agriculture to the individual, community and nation
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain the importance of agriculture to the individual, community and nation

topics.title: Problems of agricultural development and possible solutions

subtopics.content: a. Problems related to: land tenure; basic amenities; finance; transportation; storage and processing facilities; agricultural education and extension; tools and machinery; farm inputs; marketing system; environmental degradation
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify and describe the problems of agricultural development

subtopics.content: b. Possible solutions to identified problems
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to suggest possible solutions to the identified problems

topics.title: Meaning and differences between subsistence and commercial agriculture

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of subsistence and commercial agriculture
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define subsistence and commercial agriculture

subtopics.content: b. Differences between subsistence and commercial agriculture based on their characteristics
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to differentiate between subsistence and commercial agriculture

subtopics.content: c. Advantages and disadvantages of subsistence and commercial agriculture
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the advantages and disadvantages of both types

subtopics.content: d. Problems of subsistence and commercial agriculture
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss the problems of both types, including incidence of pests and diseases, vagaries of weather, labour and government policy

topics.title: Roles of government in agricultural development

subtopics.content: a. Agricultural finance: (i) credit; (ii) subsidy
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain the role of government in agricultural finance

subtopics.content: b. Agricultural education
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the role of government in agricultural education

subtopics.content: c. Agricultural extension services
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe government extension services

subtopics.content: d. Agricultural policies and programmes
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to discuss past and present programmes e.g. OFN, ADP, Farm Settlement, Agricultural Sector Rehabilitation Project (ASRP) and National Aids Coordination Secretariat

topics.title: Role of non-governmental organizations in agricultural development

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of non-governmental organizations (NGOs)
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define NGOs

subtopics.content: b. Roles of NGOs in agricultural development
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the roles of NGOs e.g. WARDA, IITA, ILCA, ICRISAT

subtopics.content: a. Land tenure systems in West Africa
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe land tenure systems in West Africa

subtopics.content: b. Government laws on land use in West Africa
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain government laws on land use, including the Land Use Act (Decree)

subtopics.content: c. Advantages and disadvantages of the Land Use Act (Decree) and reforms in West Africa
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the advantages and disadvantages of the Land Use Act and land reforms in West Africa

topics.title: Meaning and importance of agricultural ecology

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of agricultural ecology and ecosystem
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define agricultural ecology and ecosystem

subtopics.content: b. Components of farm ecosystem e.g. biotic and abiotic
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify the biotic and abiotic components of the farm ecosystem

subtopics.content: c. Interactions of the components in the terrestrial and aquatic agro-ecosystem
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe interactions of farm crops/animals with other components in mono or sole cropping, mixed cropping, mixed farming, fish ponds and forest (rain or savannah)

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of land
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define land

subtopics.content: b. Characteristics of land – free gift of nature, immobile, limited in supply etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the characteristics of land

subtopics.content: c. Uses of land: (i) agricultural purposes - crop production, wildlife conservation/game reserve, livestock production etc.; (ii) non-agricultural purposes - industry, housing, transport etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state agricultural uses (including aquaculture, forestry and apiculture) and non-agricultural uses (health centres, church/mosque, mining, recreational centres, schools and markets)

topics.title: Factors affecting land availability for agricultural purpose

subtopics.content: a. Physical factors: soil type; topography; land degradation; soil pollution
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain the physical factors affecting land availability

subtopics.content: b. Economic factors: population pressure; expansion of industries; mining/mineral exploitation; recreation/tourism
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain the economic factors affecting land availability

subtopics.content: c. Socio-cultural factors: land tenure system; religious purpose (church, mosque and shrine) etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain the socio-cultural factors affecting land availability

topics.title: Agro-allied industries and relationship between agriculture and industry

subtopics.content: a. Agro-based industries and raw materials: paper industry – pulp wood; beverage industry – cocoa, tea etc; textile industry – cotton; soap industry – oil, seeds etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify agro-based industries and their raw materials, including others e.g. leather industry – hides and skin, canning industry – meat and fish

subtopics.content: b. Relationship between agriculture and industries: agriculture provides market for industrial products e.g. farm machinery, chemicals; agriculture provides food for industrial workers
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain the relationship between agriculture and industries

topics.title: Environmental factors affecting crop and animal distribution and production

subtopics.content: a. Climatic factors e.g. rainfall, temperature, light, wind, relative humidity
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain the effect of climatic factors on crop and animal distribution and production

subtopics.content: b. Biotic factors e.g. predators, parasites, soil micro-organisms, pests, pathogens and weeds; interrelationships such as competition, parasitism, mutualism (symbiosis)
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain the effect of biotic factors and their interrelationships

subtopics.content: c. Edaphic factors: soil pH, soil texture, soil structure, soil type etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain the effect of edaphic factors

subtopics.content: a. Types of rock: igneous; sedimentary; metamorphic
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify, describe and give examples of rock types

subtopics.content: b. Processes of rock formation
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe how igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks are formed

subtopics.content: a. Factors of soil formation: the parent rock, organisms, climate, topography and time
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain the role played by each factor in soil formation

subtopics.content: b. Processes of soil formation: physical weathering; chemical weathering
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the processes of soil formation

subtopics.content: c. Soil profile development
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define soil profile, and identify, describe and state the importance of each horizon

topics.title: Types, composition and properties of soil

subtopics.content: a. Types of soil
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify types of soil and separate soil into sand, silt and clay fractions

subtopics.content: b. Chemical and biological composition of soil: soil macro and micro nutrients; soil water; soil macro-organisms; soil microbes; soil air
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the chemical and biological composition of soil

subtopics.content: c. Soil pH
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to determine soil pH and explain the causes and correction of soil acidity/alkalinity

subtopics.content: d. Physical properties of soil: soil texture; soil structure
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe physical properties including water holding capacity, porosity, capillarity and consistency

subtopics.content: a. Macro and micro nutrients; their functions and deficiency symptoms in crops
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state functions and deficiency symptoms of macro-nutrients (N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S) and micro-nutrients (Zn, Fe, Mo, Co, Bo, Cu)

subtopics.content: b. Factors affecting availability of nutrients in soil such as pH, excess of other nutrients, leaching, crop removal, oxidation and burning
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain the factors affecting nutrient availability

subtopics.content: c. Methods of replenishing lost nutrients, e.g. crop rotation, organic manuring, fertilizer application, fallowing, liming, cover-cropping
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe methods of replenishing nutrients, including types of fertilizers and methods of fertilizer application

subtopics.content: d. Nitrogen, carbon, water and phosphorus cycles
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the nitrogen, carbon and water cycles and their importance

subtopics.content: e. Organic agriculture – meaning and importance
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define organic agriculture and state its importance

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of irrigation system
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define irrigation

subtopics.content: b. Types of irrigation systems: overhead e.g. sprinkler; surface e.g. flooding, furrow/channel, basin, border; underground e.g. perforated pipes, drips
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the types of irrigation systems

subtopics.content: c. Advantages and disadvantages of irrigation systems
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the advantages and disadvantages of each system

subtopics.content: d. Importance of irrigation
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the importance of irrigation

subtopics.content: e. Problems associated with irrigation
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify problems associated with irrigation

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of drainage
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define drainage

subtopics.content: b. Importance of drainage
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the importance of drainage

subtopics.content: c. Types of drainage systems: surface drainage e.g. channel, furrow; subsurface/underground drainage
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the types of drainage systems

subtopics.content: d. Advantages and disadvantages of drainage systems
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the advantages and disadvantages of drainage systems

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of agricultural pollution
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define agricultural pollution

subtopics.content: b. Causes/sources of pollution of agricultural lands and fish ponds: excessive application of agricultural chemicals; marine and oil spillage; livestock waste and dung disposal etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify causes and sources of land/pond pollution

subtopics.content: c. Effects of land/pond pollution on farmers and agricultural productivity
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the effects of pollution and ways of minimizing land/pond pollution

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of simple farm tools
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define simple farm tools

subtopics.content: b. Types of simple farm tools - cutlass, hoe, spade, shovel etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify, describe and state the uses of each tool

subtopics.content: c. General maintenance of simple farm tools
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the maintenance of simple farm tools

subtopics.content: a. Farm machinery: tractor; bulldozer; shellers; dryers; incubators; milking machines; combine harvester etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define, identify and state the uses/functions of farm machinery and identify their different parts (engineering details not required)

subtopics.content: b. Tractor-coupled implements: ploughs; harrows; ridgers; planters; harvesters; sprayers etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify, describe and state the uses of tractor-coupled implements and identify their parts

subtopics.content: a. Reasons for maintaining farm machines
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state reasons for maintaining farm machines

subtopics.content: b. Maintenance of farm machinery: check water and oil levels regularly; carry out routine service; keep machines clean etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe maintenance practices and precautionary measures in the use of farm machinery

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of agricultural mechanization
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define agricultural mechanization

subtopics.content: b. Mechanized agricultural operations
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe mechanized operations: ploughing, harrowing, planting, harvesting, milking etc.

subtopics.content: c. Advantages and disadvantages of agricultural mechanization
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the advantages and disadvantages of mechanization

subtopics.content: d. Limitations of agricultural mechanization
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the limitations of mechanization

subtopics.content: a. Prospects of agricultural mechanization
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to suggest ways of improving mechanization such as developing less expensive machines and establishing agricultural engineering schools for personnel

subtopics.content: a. Sources of farm power
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify sources of farm power

subtopics.content: b. Advantages and disadvantages of different sources of farm power
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the advantages and disadvantages of each source

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of farm surveying
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define farm surveying

subtopics.content: b. Common survey equipment
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify common survey equipment

subtopics.content: c. Uses of farm survey equipment
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the uses of survey equipment

subtopics.content: d. Maintenance of farm survey equipment
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe maintenance of survey equipment

subtopics.content: e. Importance of farm surveying
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the importance of farm surveying

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of farm planning
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define farm planning

subtopics.content: b. Factors to be considered in farm planning
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the factors to be considered in farm planning

subtopics.content: c. Importance of farm planning
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the importance of farm planning

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of farmstead
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define farmstead

subtopics.content: b. Importance of farmstead planning
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the importance of farmstead planning

subtopics.content: c. Factors to be considered in the design of a farmstead
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain factors in farmstead design, including site selection and location of structures

subtopics.content: d. Farmstead layout
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to sketch a farm layout (engineering details not required)

subtopics.content: a. Classification of crops based on their uses e.g. cereals, pulses, roots and tubers, vegetables
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to classify crops based on their uses

subtopics.content: b. Classification based on their life cycle e.g. annual, biennial, perennial, ephemeral
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to classify crops based on life cycle

subtopics.content: c. Classification based on their morphology e.g. monocotyledonous and dicotyledonous crops
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to classify crops based on morphology

subtopics.content: Scope for each crop: botanical and common names, varieties/types, climatic and soil requirements, land preparation, methods of propagation, planting date, seed rate, spacing, sowing depth and nursery requirements, cultural practices (supplying, thinning, manuring and fertilizer requirement and application, weeding, pests and disease control), harvesting, processing and storage of at least one representative crop from each grouping below
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the husbandry of selected crops (a general knowledge of the husbandry of all crops listed is presumed)

subtopics.content: a. Cereals e.g. maize, rice, guinea corn, millet
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the husbandry of cereals

subtopics.content: b. Pulses (grain legumes) e.g. cowpea, soya bean, pigeon pea
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the husbandry of pulses

subtopics.content: c. Roots and tubers e.g. cassava, yam, potatoes
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the husbandry of roots and tubers

subtopics.content: d. Vegetables e.g. tomatoes, onion, amaranthus, okro, cauliflower, spinach
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the husbandry of vegetables

subtopics.content: e. Fruits e.g. citrus, banana, pineapple
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the husbandry of fruits

subtopics.content: f. Beverages e.g. cocoa, tea, coffee
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the husbandry of beverage crops

subtopics.content: g. Spices e.g. pepper, ginger
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the husbandry of spices

subtopics.content: h. Oils e.g. groundnut, sheabutter, sunflower, oil palm
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the husbandry of oil crops

subtopics.content: i. Fibres e.g. cotton, jute, sissal hemp
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the husbandry of fibre crops

subtopics.content: j. Latex e.g. rubber
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the husbandry of latex crops

subtopics.content: k. Others – sugar cane etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the husbandry of other crops such as sugar cane

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of pasture and forage crops
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define pasture and forage crops

subtopics.content: b. Uses of forage crops
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the uses of forage crops

subtopics.content: c. Types of pasture
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify types of pasture

subtopics.content: d. Common grasses and legumes used for grazing livestock
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the botanical names and characteristics of common grasses and legumes used for grazing

subtopics.content: e. Factors affecting the distribution and productivity of pasture
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain factors affecting distribution and productivity of pasture

subtopics.content: f. Establishment of pasture
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe how pasture is established

subtopics.content: g. Management practices of pasture
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe pasture management practices

subtopics.content: a. Aims of crop improvement
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define crop improvement and state its aims

subtopics.content: b. Methods/processes of crop improvement e.g. introduction, selection, breeding
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe methods of crop improvement

subtopics.content: c. Mendel's laws of inheritance
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define genetic terms (characters or traits, chromosomes, genes) and state Mendel's 1st and 2nd laws

subtopics.content: d. Advantages and disadvantages of crop improvement
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the advantages and disadvantages of crop improvement

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of forest and forestry
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define forest and forestry

subtopics.content: b. Importance of forestry
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the importance of forestry

subtopics.content: c. Forest regulations
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state forest regulations

subtopics.content: d. Forest management practices
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe forest management practices

subtopics.content: e. Implications of deforestation
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain the implications of deforestation

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of agro-forestry
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define agro-forestry

subtopics.content: b. Agro-forestry practices: taungya system; alley cropping; ley farming etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe agro-forestry practices and identify common tree species suitable for them

topics.title: Meaning and importance of ornamental plants

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of ornamental plants
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define ornamental plants

subtopics.content: b. Importance of ornamental plants
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the importance of ornamental plants

subtopics.content: a. Types of ornamental plants according to their uses: bedding plants (mostly flowering plants); hedging plants; lawn grasses etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify various types of ornamental plants according to their uses

subtopics.content: b. Examples of ornamental plants
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to give examples with their common and botanical names

topics.title: Settings and location for planting ornamental plants

subtopics.content: a. Settings and location for planting ornamental plants
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe suitable settings and locations for ornamental plants

subtopics.content: a. By seed
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the importance of propagation by seed and give examples of ornamental plants propagated by this method

subtopics.content: b. Vegetative propagation
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the importance of vegetative propagation and give examples of ornamental plants propagated by this method

subtopics.content: a. Maintenance of ornamental plants
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state reasons for maintenance operations such as watering, mulching and pruning

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of disease
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define disease

subtopics.content: b. General effects of diseases on crop production
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the general effects of diseases on crop production

subtopics.content: c. Disease: causal organism, economic importance, mode of transmission, symptoms, prevention and control measures of the diseases of: (i) cereals – smut, rice blast, leaf rust etc; (ii) legumes – cercospora leaf spot, rosette etc; (iii) beverages – cocoa blackpod, swollen shoot, coffee leaf rust etc; (iv) tubers – cassava mosaic, bacterial leaf blight etc; (v) fruits – citrus gummosis, dieback etc; (vi) fibre – black arm/bacterial blight of cotton etc; (vii) vegetables – root knot of tomato or okro, damping off, onion twister etc; (viii) stored produce – mould etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe diseases of crops, covering at least two fungal, two viral, two bacterial and one nematode disease of the crops chosen from the list

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of pests
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define pests

subtopics.content: b. Classification of pests: insect-pests; non-insect pests
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to classify pests

subtopics.content: c. Classification of insect-pests based on mouth parts with examples: biting and chewing; piercing and sucking; boring
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to classify insect-pests by mouth parts and give examples

subtopics.content: d. Important insect-pests of major crops (field and storage pests; life cycle, economic importance, nature of damage, preventive and control measures): (i) cereals – stem borer, army worm, ear worm etc; (ii) legumes – pod borer, aphids, sucking bugs and leaf beetle; (iii) beverages – cocoa mirids (capsids); (iv) tubers – yam beetle, cassava mealybugs, green spidermites, variegated grasshopper; (v) fibre – cotton stainer, bollworms; (vi) fruits and vegetables – thrips, grasshopper, leaf roller, leaf beetle, scale insect; (vii) stored produce – grain weevils, bean beetle
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the life cycle, nature of damage, economic importance, and preventive and control measures of the insect-pests

subtopics.content: e. Non-insect pests e.g. birds, rodents etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the nature of damage, economic importance, and preventive and control measures of non-insect pests

subtopics.content: f. Side effects of preventive and control methods: chemical – pollution, poisoning; biological – disruption of the ecosystem etc; cultural – harmful effects of burning etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the side effects of pest preventive and control methods

subtopics.content: g. General effects/economic importance of pests
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the general effects and economic importance of pests

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of weeds
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define weeds

subtopics.content: b. Types of weeds
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify types of weeds, including common and botanical names

subtopics.content: c. Effects of weeds on crops and economy
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the effects of weeds on crops and the economy

subtopics.content: d. Characteristic features of weeds
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the characteristic features of weeds

subtopics.content: e. Methods of controlling weeds: cultural, biological, chemical, physical and mechanical methods
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe methods of weed control

topics.title: Types and classification of farm animals

subtopics.content: a. Types of farm animals: cattle, sheep, goat, poultry, pig, rabbit, fish etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify types of farm animals

subtopics.content: b. Classification of farm animals according to: (i) habitat – terrestrial and aquatic; (ii) uses – food, protection, pet etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to classify farm animals by habitat and uses

topics.title: Anatomy and physiology of farm animals

subtopics.content: a. Parts of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to draw and label parts of farm animals

subtopics.content: b. Organs of farm animals e.g. heart, liver, lungs
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify important organs and state their functions

subtopics.content: c. Systems of farm animals e.g. digestive system, circulatory system, respiratory system
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe body systems, including the digestive system of poultry and differences between monogastric and ruminant digestive systems

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of reproduction
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define reproduction

subtopics.content: b. Roles of hormones in reproduction of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the roles of hormones in reproduction

subtopics.content: c. Reproductive systems of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the reproductive systems of farm animals

subtopics.content: d. Processes of reproduction in farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the processes including oestrus cycle, heat period, mating, gestation period, parturition, lactation, colostrum, mammary glands, signs of heat, ovulation etc.

subtopics.content: e. Egg formation in poultry
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe egg formation in poultry

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of environmental physiology
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define environmental physiology

subtopics.content: b. Effects of changes in climatic factors such as temperature, relative humidity and light on growth, reproduction, milk production, egg production etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain the effects of climatic factors on animal growth and production

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of livestock management
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define livestock management

subtopics.content: b. Requirements for livestock management: housing; feeding; hygiene and finishing of at least one ruminant and one non-ruminant from birth to market weight
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe extensive, intensive and semi-intensive systems of management and record keeping

subtopics.content: c. Importance of management practices
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the importance of management practices

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of animal nutrition
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define animal nutrition

subtopics.content: b. Classification of feeds
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to classify feeds

subtopics.content: c. Sources and functions of feed nutrients
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state sources and functions of feed nutrients (biochemical details not required)

subtopics.content: d. Types of ration/diet and their uses; components of a balanced diet, production and maintenance rations
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe diets for various classes of animals, their characteristics and supplementary feeding

subtopics.content: e. Causes and symptoms of malnutrition and their correction in farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe malnutrition-related conditions such as ketosis and rickets

subtopics.content: a. Meaning and importance of rangeland/pasture to livestock and the characteristics of rangeland
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define rangeland and pasture, and state their importance and characteristics

subtopics.content: b. Common grasses and legumes in rangeland
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify common grasses and legumes in rangeland

subtopics.content: c. Factors affecting the level of production of herbage: rainfall, grass/legume composition, grazing etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain factors affecting herbage production

subtopics.content: d. Methods of rangeland and pasture improvement: controlled stocking, rotational grazing, use of fertilizers, introduction of legumes, reseeding, weed control, burning, pest and disease control
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe methods of rangeland and pasture improvement

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of animal improvement
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define animal improvement

subtopics.content: b. Aims of animal improvement
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the aims of animal improvement

subtopics.content: c. Methods of animal improvement: introduction; selection; breeding
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe methods of improvement, including differences and similarities between breeds (local, exotic and cross/hybrid) and performance of animals

subtopics.content: d. Artificial insemination: (i) meaning; (ii) methods of collecting semen; (iii) advantages and disadvantages
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe artificial insemination, its methods of semen collection, and its advantages and disadvantages

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of disease
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define disease

subtopics.content: b. Causal organisms: viruses, bacteria, fungi and protozoa
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify causal organisms of animal diseases

subtopics.content: c. Factors that could predispose animals to diseases: health status of animals, nutrition, management etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the predisposing factors

subtopics.content: d. Reaction of animals to diseases: susceptibility and resistance to diseases
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain susceptibility and resistance to diseases

subtopics.content: e. Selected livestock diseases (causal organisms, symptoms, mode of transmission, effects, prevention and control): (i) viral – foot and mouth, rinderpest, newcastle; (ii) bacterial – anthrax, brucellosis, tuberculosis; (iii) fungal – aspergillosis, ringworm, scabies; (iv) protozoa – trypanosomiasis, coccidiosis
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the selected diseases and state their economic importance

subtopics.content: f. Parasites: (i) meaning of parasite; (ii) types of parasites; (iii) mode of transmission, life cycle, economic importance and control of endoparasites – tapeworm, liverfluke and roundworm; ectoparasites – ticks, lice
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the selected parasites, their life cycles, economic importance and control

subtopics.content: g. General methods of prevention and control of diseases and parasites: quarantine, inoculation/immunization, hygiene, breeding for resistance etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe general methods of preventing and controlling diseases and parasites

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of aquaculture
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define aquaculture

subtopics.content: b. Different types of aquaculture: fish farming; shrimp farming; crab farming
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify types of aquaculture

subtopics.content: c. Meaning and importance of fish farming
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define fish farming and state its importance

subtopics.content: d. Conditions necessary for siting a fish pond
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state conditions necessary for siting a fish pond

subtopics.content: e. Establishment and maintenance of fish pond
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe establishment and maintenance of a fish pond, including aeration, stocking, feeding, harvesting, processing and preservation of fish

subtopics.content: f. Fishery regulations – meaning and regulations
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state fishery regulations

subtopics.content: g. Fishing methods and tools
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe fishing methods and tools

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of apiculture or bee keeping
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define apiculture

subtopics.content: b. Types of bees: indigenous bees; exotic bees
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify types of bees

subtopics.content: c. Importance of bee keeping
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the importance of bee keeping

subtopics.content: d. Methods of bee keeping: traditional method; modern bee keeping
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe methods of bee keeping

subtopics.content: e. Bee keeping equipment: bee hives, hive tools like suits, smokers, jungle boots, brushes etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify bee keeping equipment and state their uses

subtopics.content: f. Precautionary measures in bee keeping: locate apiaries far from human dwellings; put warning symbols near apiary etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state precautionary measures in bee keeping

sections.sectionTitle: Section I: Agricultural Economics and Extension

subtopics.content: a. Scarcity
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain scarcity

subtopics.content: b. Choice
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain choice

subtopics.content: c. Scale of preference
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain scale of preference

subtopics.content: d. Law of diminishing returns
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state and explain the law of diminishing returns

subtopics.content: a. Land
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe land as a factor of production

subtopics.content: b. Capital
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe capital as a factor of production

subtopics.content: c. Labour – characteristics and classification
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe labour, including rural-urban migration and how it affects labour availability in agricultural production

subtopics.content: d. Management or entrepreneur
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe management as a factor of production

subtopics.content: a. Definition of demand
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define demand

subtopics.content: b. Law of demand
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the law of demand

subtopics.content: c. Factors affecting demand for agricultural produce
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain factors affecting demand

subtopics.content: d. Movements along the demand curve
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain movements along the demand curve

subtopics.content: e. Shifts in the demand curve
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain shifts in the demand curve

subtopics.content: a. Definition of supply
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define supply

subtopics.content: b. Law of supply
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the law of supply

subtopics.content: c. Movements along supply curve
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain movements along the supply curve

subtopics.content: d. Shifts in the supply curve
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain shifts in the supply curve

subtopics.content: e. Factors affecting the supply of agricultural produce
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain factors affecting supply

topics.title: Implications of demand and supply for agricultural production

subtopics.content: a. Price support
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain price support

subtopics.content: b. Price control
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain price control

subtopics.content: c. Subsidy programme and its effects on agricultural production
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain subsidy programmes and their effects

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of a farm manager
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define a farm manager and farm management

subtopics.content: b. Functions of a farm manager
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the functions of a farm manager

subtopics.content: a. Problems faced by farm managers
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify problems faced by farm managers, including the meaning of agri-business

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of agricultural finance
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define agricultural finance

subtopics.content: b. Importance of agricultural finance
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state its importance

subtopics.content: c. Sources of farm finance
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify sources of farm finance

subtopics.content: d. Classes of farm credit: (i) based on length of time – short-term, medium-term, long-term; (ii) based on source – institutional, non-institutional; (iii) based on liquidity – loan in-cash, loan in-kind
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to classify farm credit

subtopics.content: e. Problems faced by farmers in procuring agricultural credit - high interest rate; lack or inadequate collateral etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state problems farmers face in procuring credit

subtopics.content: f. Problems faced by institutions in granting loans to farmers - lack of records and accounts etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state problems institutions face in granting loans

subtopics.content: g. Capital market: (i) meaning of capital market and institutions that deal with medium and long term loans for agricultural business; (ii) institutions involved in the capital market; (iii) sources of funds for the capital market – bonds, insurance companies, merchant banks, the stock exchange (sales and purchases of shares); (iv) roles of capital markets in agricultural business – mobilization of long term funds for on-lending, reducing over reliance on money market etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the capital market, its institutions, sources of funds and roles in agricultural business

subtopics.content: a. Importance of farm records
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the importance of farm records

subtopics.content: b. Types of farm records: inventory records; production records; income and expenditure records; supplementary or special records
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe types of farm records

subtopics.content: c. Designing farm records
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to design farm records

subtopics.content: d. Farm accounts: expenditure/purchases account; income/sales account; profit and loss account; balance sheet
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to prepare farm accounts and use terms such as salvage value, appreciation, farm budget, depreciation and inventory to calculate profit and loss of crops, livestock, machinery and tools

subtopics.content: a. Meaning and importance of marketing of agricultural produce
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define marketing and state its importance

subtopics.content: b. Marketing agents and their functions
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the functions, advantages and disadvantages of marketing agents

subtopics.content: c. Marketing functions: assembling; transportation; processing etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe marketing functions

subtopics.content: d. Marketing of export crops
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe the marketing of export crops

subtopics.content: e. Export crops in West Africa
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify export crops in West Africa

subtopics.content: f. Guidelines for exporting crops in West Africa
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state guidelines for exporting crops

subtopics.content: g. Corporate bodies, cooperative societies and individuals engaged in exporting agricultural produce e.g. ANCE - Association of Nigerian Cooperative Exporters
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify bodies engaged in exporting agricultural produce

subtopics.content: h. Importance of exporting agricultural produce
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state the importance of exporting agricultural produce

subtopics.content: i. Problems of marketing agricultural produce
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify problems of marketing agricultural produce

subtopics.content: a. Meaning of agricultural insurance
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define agricultural insurance

subtopics.content: b. Importance of agricultural insurance
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to state its importance

subtopics.content: c. Types of insurance policies for agricultural production: specific enterprise insurance e.g. crop insurance, livestock insurance; farm vehicle insurance; fire disaster insurance or machines and buildings insurance; life assurance (farmers, farm workers and farmers' household)
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe types of insurance policies

subtopics.content: d. Insurance premium
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to explain insurance premium

subtopics.content: e. Problems of agricultural insurance: uncertainties of weather; losses due to natural disaster etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify problems of agricultural insurance

subtopics.content: a. Meaning and importance of agricultural extension
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to define agricultural extension and state its importance, including qualities of a good extension worker

subtopics.content: b. Agricultural extension methods: individual contact methods; group contact methods etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe extension methods

subtopics.content: c. Agricultural extension programmes in West Africa e.g. ADP, NDE, Agro-service centres, state ministries of agriculture and natural resources
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe extension programmes in West Africa

subtopics.content: d. Problems of agricultural extension in West Africa e.g. illiteracy among farmers, inadequate transport facilities etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify problems of agricultural extension

subtopics.content: 1. Soil
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to examine soil samples for texture by manual feeling of wet and dry soil, and examine fertile and infertile soils noting colour, texture, structure, presence of organic matter and living things

subtopics.content: 2. Soil profile
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe and identify a simple soil profile

subtopics.content: 3. Rocks
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify common rock types: igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic

subtopics.content: 4. Laboratory work on physical properties of soil: (a) mechanical analysis by sedimentation and by hydrometer method or sieves; (b) determination of bulk density and total pore space; (c) determination of moisture content of a moist soil sample; (d) determination of maximum water holding capacity; (e) determination of wilting point; (f) determination of capillary action
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to carry out laboratory determinations of the physical properties of soil

subtopics.content: 5. Laboratory work on chemical properties of soil: (a) determination of soil acidity using pH meter and/or any other gadget or simple equipment; (b) common types of chemical fertilizers; (d) organic manure: green manure, farm yard, compost
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to determine soil pH, identify fertilizers (N, P, K and compound) with methods and rates of application, and identify, prepare and apply compost

subtopics.content: 6. Irrigation and drainage
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify irrigation and drainage equipment and state their uses e.g. watering can, sprinkler, pump, pipes

subtopics.content: 1. Farm tools and equipment
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify, describe, use and maintain garden tools e.g. hoe, cutlass, garden trowel, hand fork, shovel, spade, rake, sickle, secateurs, shears, long handle hoe, pruner, budding knife, emasculator

subtopics.content: 2. Tractor and animal drawn implement
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify, describe, use and maintain tractor and animal-drawn implements e.g. ploughs, harrows, ridgers, planters, cultivators, and identify their major parts and functions

subtopics.content: 3. Harvesting, processing and storage equipment
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify, describe and state uses of equipment e.g. dehuskers, shellers, winnowers, dryers, processors, graters, refrigerators, cutlasses, scythe, groundnut lifters

subtopics.content: 4. Farm tractor
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify the major components of the farm tractor and describe its servicing and maintenance

subtopics.content: 5. Uses and maintenance of horticultural tools and implements
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify, use and maintain shears, dibber, pruning knife, secateurs, budding knife, measuring tapes, hand fork, hand trowel, hoe and fork

subtopics.content: 6. Livestock and fishing equipment
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify, describe, use and care for equipment e.g. waterers, feeders, milking machines, nets, hook and line, branding machine, egg candler

subtopics.content: 7. Farm surveying equipment
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify, use and care for equipment e.g. measuring tape, pins or arrows, ranging poles, plum bob, offset staff, compass, gunter's chains, pegs, theodolite

subtopics.content: 1. Seeds, seedlings, fruits and storage organs of crops
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify seeds, seedlings, fruits, storage organs and essential parts of common crop plants, pasture grasses and legumes

subtopics.content: 2. Main pests and diseases of crops
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify main field and storage pests (e.g. cotton stainer, yam beetles, weevils) and the damage they cause, and main crop diseases, their causal agents, symptoms, prevention and control

subtopics.content: 3. Planting dates, seed rates, plant population and seed quality tests of the more common local crop plants
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to determine planting dates, seed rates, plant population and carry out seed quality tests

subtopics.content: 4. Preparation of seedbeds, fertilizer application, mulching, use of pesticides, watering, vegetative propagation, germination tests etc.
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to perform these operations, including propagation methods: direct sowing, transplanting, layering, grafting and budding

subtopics.content: 5. Forest products and by-products
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify forest products and by-products

subtopics.content: 6. Methods of propagation of horticultural plants
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe methods of propagation of horticultural plants

subtopics.content: 7. Common weeds
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify common weeds, their external features, mode of dispersal and methods of control on the farm

subtopics.content: 1. Common breeds of animals and types of animals available in the locality
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify breeds, and carry out restraint, handling and grooming of farm animals

subtopics.content: 2. Major internal organs of farm animals, e.g. organs of the digestive system, reproductive and excretory systems
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify the major internal organs and state their functions

subtopics.content: 3. Animal by-products
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify animal by-products e.g. hides and skin, fur, feather, horn

subtopics.content: 4. Animal feeds and feed stuffs and their local sources
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify feeds and feed stuffs (e.g. fish meal, groundnut cake, rice bran), state their uses and types of diets/rations

subtopics.content: 5. Main pests and parasites of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify common ectoparasites (e.g. ticks, lice) and endoparasites (e.g. tapeworms, liver flukes, roundworms), the damage caused, their control and their life cycles

subtopics.content: 6. Diseases of farm animals
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe methods of prevention and control e.g. drugging, drenching, dipping, spraying and simple farm sanitation

subtopics.content: 7. Routine management practices in farm animals, e.g. selection of livestock and poultry for breeding, culling, ear-notching, tattooing, horn or skin branding, debeaking, dehorning, castration
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to identify equipment/tools used for routine management practices

subtopics.content: 8. Fish harvesting and preservation
subtopics.objective: Candidates should be able to describe methods of harvesting, processing and preservation of fish
